resolved_by: The Supreme Court resolved the split in Dean v. United States (2017), which the opinion says settled a circuit split on the sentencing discretion a district court may exercise when a § 924(c) mandatory minimum runs alongside a sentence for the predicate offense.
issue: May a district court, when sentencing a defendant for a predicate offense alongside a § 924(c) mandatory minimum, consider the § 924(c) sentence in setting the predicate sentence?

sides.position: Pre-Dean rule: the district court was precluded from exercising the sentencing discretion at issue.
cases: United States v. Dean, 810 F.3d 521 (8th Cir. 2015)

quote: Put diﬀerently, it took the Supreme Court deciding Dean to reveal the error in the Eighth Circuit’s law, settle a circuit split, and announce a new rule.
cite: John Worman v. Frederick Entzel, 953 F.3d 1004 (7th Cir. 2020)
